concepts.name: Receptors, neurons and nerve impulses
concepts.description: Receptors at the tips of nerve cells, mostly in sense organs, detect information; impulses pass dendrite -> cell body -> axon; nervous tissue conducts information as electrical impulses.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.1, p.101 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Synapse
concepts.description: At the end of an axon the electrical impulse releases chemicals that cross the gap (synapse) and start an impulse in the next neuron, or deliver it to muscle or gland cells.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.1, p.101 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Reflex actions and the reflex arc
concepts.description: A reflex is a quick response made without thinking; the reflex arc links input and output nerves in the spinal cord, which is faster than waiting for the brain, although the input still reaches the brain.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.1.1, p.102-103 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Human brain and nervous system
concepts.description: Brain and spinal cord form the central nervous system, cranial and spinal nerves the peripheral one; the fore-brain thinks and decides, the medulla in the hind-brain controls involuntary actions; skull, fluid and vertebral column protect them.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.1.2-6.1.3, p.103-105 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Cerebellum
concepts.description: The cerebellum, part of the hind-brain, is responsible for the precision of voluntary actions and for keeping posture and balance (walking straight, riding a bicycle, picking up a pencil).
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.1.2, p.104 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: How muscles move
concepts.description: Muscle tissue does the final job of movement: in response to nerve impulses, special proteins in muscle cells change shape and arrangement so the cells shorten; voluntary and involuntary muscles.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.1.4, p.105 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Plant movements and tropisms
concepts.description: Plants move without nerves or muscles: the sensitive plant folds its leaves without growth (cells change water content), while tendrils and tropisms (photo-, geo-, chemo-, hydrotropism) are directional growth movements.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.2-6.2.2, p.105-107 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Plant hormones
concepts.description: Plant hormones are made away from where they act and diffuse there: auxin moves to the shady side so the shoot bends towards light; gibberellins and cytokinins promote growth; abscisic acid inhibits it.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.2.2, p.108 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Hormones in animals
concepts.description: Endocrine glands secrete hormones into the blood: adrenaline (adrenal glands) prepares the body for emergencies, thyroxin needs iodine, growth hormone (pituitary), testosterone and oestrogen at puberty, insulin (pancreas).
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.3, p.109-110 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Feedback control of hormones
concepts.description: Hormones must be secreted in precise amounts; feedback mechanisms regulate the timing and amount (e.g. rising blood sugar leads the pancreas to make more insulin), and the hypothalamus releases releasing factors.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §6.3, p.110-111 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)
